req.title: Update existing post
req.statement: The system shall update the row when POST /<id>/update is called by the post's author with a title and body, and redirect to /.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that POST /<id>/update by the post's author with valid title and body must update the DB row and return 302 to /. I need: (1) a positive EP test confirming the happy path updates the row and redirects; (2) a negative NEG test for a non-author attempting the update (403); (3) a BVA boundary test using a single-character title (minimum valid length); (4) a DT test for missing title (empty string) which should NOT update and should stay on the form; (5) a STC test verifying the state transition from pre-update to post-update values in the DB; (6) a NEG test for unauthenticated access (302 to login). Each test is self-contained with its own app/db setup.

tests.name: test_update_post_happy_path_redirects_and_persists
preconditions: App initialized with test DB containing seeded data
User Rahul (id=1) is logged in
Post id=2 exists and is authored by Rahul (author_id=1)
actions: POST /2/update with title='Updated Title' and body='Updated body text'
expected: DB row for post id=2 has title='Updated Title' and body='Updated body text'
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

def test_update_post_happy_path_redirects_and_persists():
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    r = client.post('/2/update', data={'title': 'Updated Title', 'body': 'Updated body text'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'
    with app.app_context():
        db = get_db()
        row = db.execute('SELECT title, body FROM post WHERE id = 2').fetchone()
        assert row['title'] == 'Updated Title'
        assert row['body'] == 'Updated body text'

tests.name: test_update_post_state_transition_old_to_new_values
preconditions: App initialized with test DB containing seeded data
User Rahul (id=1) is logged in
Post id=6 exists with title='Srism vector cascade' authored by Rahul
actions: Verify pre-update state: title='Srism vector cascade'
POST /6/update with title='New Title State' and body='New body state'
Verify post-update state: title='New Title State'
expected: Pre-update title is exactly 'Srism vector cascade'
Post-update title is exactly 'New Title State'
Post-update body is exactly 'New body state'
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

def test_update_post_state_transition_old_to_new_values():
    with app.app_context():
        db = get_db()
        pre = db.execute('SELECT title, body FROM post WHERE id = 6').fetchone()
        assert pre['title'] == 'Srism vector cascade'
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    r = client.post('/6/update', data={'title': 'New Title State', 'body': 'New body state'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'
    with app.app_context():
        db = get_db()
        post = db.execute('SELECT title, body FROM post WHERE id = 6').fetchone()
        assert post['title'] == 'New Title State'
        assert post['body'] == 'New body state'
